name: Hepatocyte (liver cell)
short_description: Polyhedral liver cell, ~25 µm across and often binucleate, packed with smooth and rough ER, mitochondria and peroxisomes. It detoxifies blood, breaks down medicines, makes bile and plasma proteins, and stores sugar as glycogen; one face borders a blood sinusoid, the opposite face forms a tiny bile canal shared with its neighbour.

Almost no clean background left for labels)

The neighbour is now a plain partial strip, not a mirror copy. No text, no border, no vignette)

3d.2: pass (gemini-2.5-flash-image; the geometry corrections landed. A chunky polyhedral cell with soft global illumination and subsurface scattering, bordered on the left by an open dusky-red sinusoid lane running off the top and bottom of frame with fenestration pores and a rim-lit microvillar fringe; on the right an olive-yellow bile-canaliculus slot in the seam with the neighbour, lined with short microvilli. Interior in natural biological tints — two staggered nuclei with nucleoli, pink rough-ER slabs, a green smooth-ER mesh, cristate mitochondria, teal peroxisomes, violet lysosomes, turquoise Golgi crescents, orange glycogen rosettes and cream lipid droplets. Not near-monochrome, not neon. Clean dark studio background, no border, no text)

reference: pass (Wikimedia Commons — 'Hepatocitos.jpg', a genuine high-power H&E section of liver, CC BY-SA 4.0, Aigaby. Verified by eye: polyhedral hepatocytes in plates one cell thick, narrow sinusoids with flattened endothelial nuclei, large euchromatic nuclei with prominent nucleoli, and several unambiguously binucleate hepatocytes. No baked-in text, scale bar or border in the source. Cleaned with edit_image.py (real-02) to crop slightly tighter on a readable field while keeping the H&E colorization and inventing nothing; the original download real-01 is kept for provenance and is essentially equivalent. Honest caveat: the uploader does not state the species, so it is captioned 'liver, H&E' rather than 'human liver')
decision: use as final and as the SVG label base; the only render that gets all three hard points right at once — polyhedral shape, visible binucleation, and the two different faces (sinusoid + microvilli vs. bile-canaliculus groove between neighbours)
